Maya (sec-eng): Quick prep for GreenHarbor onboarding call in 45m. They want two pockets of detail: 1) what we can hand them during an incident for forensic timelines, 2) how BYO-KMS + key rotation works w/ our backups. Keep replies short.
Sam (GreenHarbor): first, does your audit export preserve monotonic timestamps? our legal wants deterministic timelines across services.
Nate (eng-sre): We store events with UTC epoch nanos and a monotonic sequence id per request. Exports include both fields so you can order even if clocks drift.
Liu (infra): For BYO-KMS: we use envelope encryption. We never hold plaintext master keys; we hold encrypted DEKs wrapped to the customer KEK. Rotation = rewrap flow.
Sam (GreenHarbor): If we rotate KEK, can you decrypt historical payloads? what about cached DEKs in runtime nodes?
Maya (sec-eng): Yes, historical DEKs remain wrapped under old KEKs for a configurable rewrap retention. Runtime nodes purge cached DEKs after TTL; during rotation we recommend a rewrap window (default 14 days) and a short live cache TTL (1h) to reduce exposure.
Priya (acct-mgr): Customer-facing: put rotation window and cache TTL in onboarding doc; security addendum to cover custom retention.
Sam (GreenHarbor): They also want signed evidence packages for incidents with a verifiable chain. Is that available?
Nate (eng-sre): We can produce a signed archive (.tar.gz + detached sig) signed by an HSM-backed signing key. The manifest includes hash-chain for each file.
Maya (sec-eng): Example manifest snippet: 
```
{
  "export_time": "2026-05-01T15:04:05Z",
  "files": ["auth.jsonl.gz","kms_events.jsonl.gz","api_traces.jsonl.gz"],
  "chain_hash": "sha256:abcdef..."
}
```
Sam (GreenHarbor): They use Splunk and QRadar. Can you stream to their SIEM? format?
Liu (infra): We stream via TLS in JSONL (newline-delimited JSON). For CEF we can provide a sidecar formatter, but JSONL is standard. Compression is gzip; schema v2 docs linked.
Maya (sec-eng): Also asked about RBAC: they want to delegate limited KMS decrypt rights to service accounts scoped to tenant resources for emergency decrypts.
Nate (eng-sre): We recommend never giving tenant users direct KMS decrypt on customer KEKs. Instead create a short-lived Engine role with AssumeRole + PrincipalTag filter. Example policy: 
```
allow: kms:Decrypt
resource: arn:cloud:kms:region:acct:key/REDACTED
condition: tag:tenant_id=="greenharbor"
```
This role is issued to our runtime during a step-up with audit and TTL.
Sam (GreenHarbor): Ok. One more: vuln triage during incident 10xx CVE flagged in runtime. Do you share repro steps and patch ETA?
Maya (sec-eng): We'll share triage notes, affected versions, mitigation steps, and planned patch ETA under NDA. For zero-days we coordinate an embargoed timeline and provide an IR pack after disclosure.
zapier-bot: Reminder  export-template-grant created by Priya: https://redwood.internal/export-templates/gh.json
Priya (acct-mgr): Action items: Liu produce signed export example + manifest sample (due 3pm); Nate produce SIEM sample payloads (Splunk/CEF) + retention note (due EOD); Maya draft onboarding snippet and security addendum text (due EOD). I'll circulate to Sam before the call.
Sam (GreenHarbor): Perfect  will confirm call invite and compliance attendees. Thanks!
Maya (sec-eng): Great  keep answers concrete, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
